cohort: 86 patients with placental abruption and matched controls who delivered at Tuen Mun Hospital in Hong Kong
finding: Placental abruption was associated with a higher rate of cesarean sections, postpartum hemorrhage, uterine atony, blood transfusion, and disseminated intravascular coagulopathy, as well as lower Apgar scores, higher preterm birth rate, lower birth weight, and more perinatal morbidities in neonates.
mod_finding: Placental abruption was associated with a higher rate of cesarean sections.
birth_weight: Lower in neonates complicated with placental abruption (2296.4 g vs 3088.8 g)
